title: PR gnostic sandbox notes
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a lightweight, model-agnostic ("gnostic") PR review heuristic I want to prototype when I'm short on time. Idea: produce a 0–5 risk / readiness score with specific short evidence bits so reviewers and on-call understand the main tradeoffs quickly.

Goal:
- Fast, repeatable assessment for small-to-medium PRs (<= 600 LOC) that might touch serving runtime, routing, or batching logic.
- Surface a small set of actionable follow-ups instead of a long narrative.
- Capture rollback criteria and quick mitigation steps so releases aren't blocked.

How to use (mental model):
- Read changed files and tests; run staging smoke tests (2–3 commands).
- For each rubric item below, note 0/1/2 (low/medium/high concern). Sum to make a 0–10 raw score, map to 0–5.
- Attach 3-line summary to PR: score, top-2 risks, one immediate mitigation.

Lightweight rubric (evidence-first):
1) Surface-change footprint (0: pure docs/tests, 1: localized refactor, 2: infra/runtime hotpath)
2) Safety nets & tests (0: tests + e2e, 1: unit tests only, 2: no tests or flaky)
3) Observability impact (0: new metrics/traces/logs added, 1: no change, 2: removes/obscures logs)
4) Backwards-compat (0: fully compatible, 1: opt-in change, 2: breaking by default)
5) Rollback complexity (0: trivial revert and redeploy, 1: requires migration/coord, 2: cross-service rollback)

Scoring map (example):
- raw 0–1 -> score 0 (safe)
- raw 2–3 -> score 1
- raw 4–5 -> score 2
- raw 6–7 -> score 3
- raw 8 -> score 4
- raw 9–10 -> score 5 (high risk)

Quick review checklist (3–8 minute pass):
- Run local smoke: ./scripts/smoke-serving.sh --short (expect: no error in 30s)
- Check CI matrix: any nightly-only test failures?
- Are new metrics exposed? If not, flag for an observability follow-up.
- Search logs for "deprecated"/"unsafe" usage in diffs.
- Verify config flags: defaults should preserve behavior unless explicitly marked.

Micro-refactor suggestions (what to call out on PR):
- Break function with >80 LOC into smaller helpers (name suggestions in-line).
- Replace magic constant with named config + TODO to surface as runtime flag.
- Replace explicit sleeps in tests with event-driven wait (prefer trace-based sync).

Followups & tickets (placeholders I create while reviewing):
- INF-PR-SANDBOX-1: add tracing for new batching path (owner: Aisha)
- INF-PR-SANDBOX-2: add e2e that runs short LLM request patterns (owner: Lyn)
- INF-PR-SANDBOX-3: add canary rollout plan + rollback doc in product console (owner: platform-eng)

Rollback criteria (explicit, copyable into PR):
- Rollback if error rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes on canary (primary metric: polymer.kv_cache_errors)
- Rollback if p95 latency increases > 30% for 5 minutes (request path: /v1/generate)
- Manual rollback if any customer-facing SPOF is introduced (e.g., single region routing lock)

Signals to watch post-merge (first 60 min):
- Uncaught exceptions in logs with stack trace keywords from diff (grep for changed symbols)
- Sudden change in token/sec throughput in canary machines (watch dashboard: canary/batch-usage)
- CI flaky test that started failing consistently (trigger quick revert)

Commands & quick checks I run: (place these as copy-paste on PR)
- ./devctl run smoke --pr=4127 --short
- curl -s -X POST "http://staging.local/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"smoke"}' | jq '.status'
- git checkout $PR_HEAD && scripts/profile-one-req.sh

Notes to self (informal):
- If change touches kv-cache eviction, make sure to add a guard metric and default to previous behavior via feature flag.
- Don't get into long design debate in the PR; mark design questions "design: followup" and file ticket.
- For latency-sensitive paths, prefer path-preserving refactors; tiny allocations can add up at 1000 rps.

Open questions (things to ask author in PR comment):
- Why was the non-blocking queue replaced with blocking call? (risk: head-of-line blocking)
- Can we add a small microbenchmark rather than just unit tests?
- If this changes default config, were customers communicated?

Example 3-line summary to paste on PR: 
Score: 3/5 (medium) — Footprint: runtime hotpath (1), Tests: unit only (1), Observability: none (1) 
Top risks: p95 latency regression; missing canary metrics.
Immediate mitigation: add guard metric + opt-in flag; request platform to run 10-min canary before broad rollout.

Todo (short):
- [ ] Post INF-PR-SANDBOX-1 ticket (today)
- [ ] Add minimal e2e for canary path
- [ ] If author OK, push tiny helper refactor and re-run smoke

Thoughts about how this differs from existing checklists:
- Emphasis on short evidence bullets that can be machine-extracted later (e.g., tag lines: FOOTPRINT:runtime;TESTS:unit;OBSERVABILITY:none)
- Make rollback criteria explicit and copy-pasteable so on-call isn't guessing
- Keep suggestions minimal and actionable — prefer small followups over long redesigns in a single PR

End of notes.

-- Lyn
